title: Clothes shopping: sizes, colors, and trying on
title_target: ຊື້ເສື້ອຜ້າ — Sʉ̂ʉ sʉ̂a-phàa
goal: Buy clothes and shoes: ask for another size, try things on, say something is too tight or too long, and exchange the wrong item — while picking up the size adjectives used everywhere.

dialogs.title: ບົດສົນທະນາ — At a clothing shop, Talat Sao, second floor
dialogs.intro: Budi is looking for a shirt for a work event. Notice that the size adjectives always stand alone as complete sentences — no verb needed at all.

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂາຍ:
lines.text: [ສະບາຍດີ|Sa-baai-dii] [ຫາ|Hǎa][ຫຍັງ|nyǎng][ຢູ່|yùu]
lines.id: Hello. What are you looking for?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຫາ|Hǎa][ເສື້ອ|sʉ̂a][ແຂນ|khěen][ຍາວ|nyáao] [ມີ|Míi][ສີ|sǐi][ຂາວ|khǎao][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: A long-sleeved shirt. Do you have a white one?
lines.literal: look-for — shirt — sleeve — long. have — color — white — (question)?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂາຍ:
lines.text: [ມີ|Míi] [ໂຕ|Tǒo][ນີ້|nîi][ດີ|dii] [ຂະໜາດ|Kha-nàat][ໃດ|dai]
lines.id: Yes. This one's nice. What size?
lines.literal: have. piece — this — good. size — which?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ບໍ່|bàw][ຮູ້|hûu] [ລອງ|Lawng][ໃສ່|sài][ໄດ້|dâi][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: I don't know. Can I try it on?
lines.literal: I — not — know. try — wear — can — (question)?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂາຍ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi][ເລີຍ|lóei] [ຫ້ອງ|Hàwng][ລອງ|lawng][ຢູ່|yùu][ຫຼັງ|lǎng][ພຸ້ນ|phûn]
lines.id: Of course. The fitting room is back there.
lines.literal: can — right-away. room — try — be-at — back — over-there.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຄັບ|Khap][ໜ້ອຍ|nàwy][ໜຶ່ງ|nʉ̀ng] [ມີ|Míi][ໃຫຍ່|nyài][ກວ່າ|kwàa][ນີ້|nîi][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: It's a bit tight. Do you have a bigger one?
lines.literal: tight — little — one. have — big — more — this — (question)?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂາຍ:
lines.text: [ມີ|Míi] [ໂຕ|Tǒo][ນີ້|nîi][ເອວ|ée-ǎw][ໃຫຍ່|nyài][ກວ່າ|kwàa] [ລອງ|Lawng][ເບິ່ງ|bòeng][ອີກ|ìik]
lines.id: Yes. This one is roomier. Try it again.
lines.literal: have. piece — this — waist — big — more. try — see — again.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ອັນ|An][ນີ້|nîi][ພໍ|phaw][ດີ|dii] [ແຕ່|Tèe][ແຂນ|khěen][ຍາວ|nyáao][ໄປ|pai][ໜ້ອຍ|nàwy][ໜຶ່ງ|nʉ̀ng]
lines.id: This one fits. But the sleeves are a bit too long.
lines.literal: piece — this — enough — good. but — sleeve — long — over — little — one.

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂາຍ:
lines.text: [ພັບ|Pháp][ຂຶ້ນ|khʉ̂n][ໄດ້|dâi] [ຫຼື|Lʉ̌ʉ][ຊິ|si][ຕັດ|tát][ໃຫ້|hài][ກໍ|kaw][ໄດ້|dâi] [ບໍ່|Bàw][ຄິດ|khit][ເງິນ|ngóen][ຕື່ມ|tʉ̀ʉm]
lines.id: You can roll them up. Or we can shorten them for you, no extra charge.
lines.literal: fold — up — can. or — will — cut — give — also — can. not — count — money — add.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ຂອບໃຈ|Khàwp-jai] [ເອົາ|Ao][ໂຕ|tǒo][ນີ້|nîi] [ເທົ່າໃດ|Thao-dai]
lines.id: Thank you. I'll take this one. How much?

lines.speaker: ຄົນຂາຍ:
lines.text: [ໜຶ່ງ|Nʉ̀ng][ແສນ|sěen][ຊາວ|saao][ພັນ|phán] [ຖ້າ|Thàa][ບໍ່|bàw][ພໍດີ|phaw-dii] [ເອົາ|ao][ມາ|maa][ປ່ຽນ|pìan][ໄດ້|dâi][ໃນ|nai][ເຈັດ|jét][ມື້|mʉ̂ʉ]
lines.id: A hundred and twenty thousand. If it doesn't fit, you can exchange it within seven days.
lines.literal: one — hundred-thousand — twenty — thousand. if — not — fit — take — come — change — can — within — seven — day.

notes: **ລອງ lawng = "try", and it goes IN FRONT of the verb.** *ລອງໃສ່* (try on), *ລອງເບິ່ງ* (try and see), *ລອງກິນ* (try eating). On its own, *ລອງເບິ່ງ lawng bòeng* means "give it a try" for anything.

**ຄັບ khap = "tight", ຫຼວມ lǔam = "loose".** Both are for clothes only. For a cramped space the word is different: *ແຄບ khêep*. ⚠️ Don't confuse it with Thai *ครับ khráp*, the polite particle — in Lao, *ຄັບ* really does mean tight.
**ພໍດີ phaw-dii = "just right, fits".** This is the word you say as soon as something fits. *ພໍດີເລີຍ* = fits perfectly. It also works for time: *ມາພໍດີ* (came just in time).

**ໄປ pai after an adjective = "too", remember from unit 8.** *ຍາວໄປ* (too long), *ສັ້ນໄປ* (too short), *ໃຫຍ່ໄປ* (too big). Adding *ໜ້ອຍໜຶ່ງ nàwy nʉ̀ng* softens it to "a bit": *ຍາວໄປໜ້ອຍໜຶ່ງ* (a bit too long).
**…ກວ່ານີ້ kwàa nîi = "more … than this", an essential shopping phrase.** *ໃຫຍ່ກວ່ານີ້* (bigger than this), *ຖືກກວ່ານີ້* (cheaper than this), *ສີອື່ນ* (another color).
**ຂະໜາດ kha-nàat = "size".** Shops in Laos use S, M, L, XL, said with English sounds: *ເອັມ em*, *ແອວ eeo*. Shoe sizes are European numbers.

**ປ່ຽນ pìan = "exchange, change".** *ເອົາມາປ່ຽນ* (bring back to exchange), *ປ່ຽນເປັນສີດຳ* (change to black). To return something for a refund, it's *ຄືນເງິນ khʉ́ʉn ngóen* — but be warned, at markets that rarely works.

**ໃສ່ sài shows up again, now meaning "wear" clothes.** *ໃສ່ເສື້ອ* (wear a shirt), *ໃສ່ເກີບ* (wear shoes), *ໃສ່ແວ່ນຕາ* (wear glasses). It's the same word you use at a food stall for "put in" ingredients.

**On dress in Laos.** For government offices, temples, and formal events, Lao women wear the *ສິ້ນ sîn* — a long woven skirt — and female guests are expected to as well. Covered shoulders and covered knees are the unwritten rule at every temple, for men and women alike.

after: The pattern *ຫາ…ຢູ່ hǎa… yùu* ("I'm looking for…") is the most natural reply to a seller's greeting. Without *ຢູ່* at the end, it sounds like an order.

blocks.text: Every word in this table stands alone as a complete sentence. *ຄັບ* already means "it's tight", *ພໍດີ* already means "it fits". There is no "is" to add — one of the things that makes Lao feel so quick to use.
To show degree, attach a word after it: *ໜ້ອຍໜຶ່ງ* (a bit), *ຫຼາຍ* (very), *ໄປ / ໂພດ* (too), *ທີ່ສຸດ* (most). A graded example: *ໃຫຍ່ໜ້ອຍໜຶ່ງ* → *ໃຫຍ່* → *ໃຫຍ່ຫຼາຍ* → *ໃຫຍ່ໂພດ*.

blocks.text: If you want to be sure something is truly hand-woven, ask *ເຮັດດ້ວຍມືບໍ່ hét dûay mʉʉ bàw* (handmade?). The word **ດ້ວຍ *dûay*** means "with, by (means of)": *ຂຽນດ້ວຍມື* (write by hand), *ໄປດ້ວຍລົດເມ* (go by bus).

**ຂອງຝາກ *khǎwng-fàak*** (gifts from a trip) is a real social obligation in Laos. Coming back from a trip with nothing for your coworkers will be noticed — and it doesn't have to be expensive, it just has to be there.
